article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Buffalo ground out a 23-6 win in Minnesota on Monday night, Week 10 opens Thursday at MetLife, and the app board still shows last week's cards — here is what changed overnight and how to use it.

items.headline: Lead: Bills grind out a 23-6 win in Minnesota, and the Vikings' quarterback problem is now the story
paragraphs: Buffalo beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night to close Week 9. It was not pretty. The Bills held the ball for 42 minutes and 32 seconds, forced three turnovers, and wore the Vikings down — James Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards and a late touchdown.

The Vikings' offense never got going. Carson Wentz started with Kyler Murray out, and he completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions. Minnesota has now lost two straight after starting 6-0, and the loss knocked the Vikings out of first place in the NFC North. Buffalo is 7-1.

For bettors, the night's numbers held up. The Bills closed at -3.5 and won by 17, so the favorite covered. The total closed at 45.5 and the game finished at 29 combined points, so the under cashed easily. Week 9 is done — the next game is Thursday night.
items.takeaway: Bills 23, Vikings 6 — Buffalo covered -3.5 and the total went well under 45.5, while Wentz's 8-for-25 night leaves Minnesota's quarterback spot wide open.

items.headline: Injuries: Darnold ruled out, Lock starts again; Cardinals turn to a rookie; McCarthy trending to play Thursday
paragraphs: Seattle's quarterback spot is settled for Week 10, and it is not good news. Sam Darnold is ruled out of Sunday's game at Las Vegas with a quadriceps injury and a cracked rib. Drew Lock starts again — he led the Seahawks to a 17-3 win over Arizona on Sunday — but Lock is managing an oblique injury and elbow tendinitis himself. Darnold is expected back after the Week 11 bye, in Week 12.

Arizona is in a worse spot. Gardner Minshew tore a UCL and may be done for the season. The Cardinals signed 40-year-old Josh Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad as the backup, and rookie Carson Beck is slated to start Week 10 against the Rams.

Thursday's game has the one name still to be confirmed. Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy hurt his hip in Sunday's win over the Eagles, missed part of the game, and came back. Head coach John Harbaugh says McCarthy is trending toward playing Thursday night against Washington.

Two more quarterback notes. Cleveland's Deshaun Watson has been cleared to play Sunday against Houston after missing last week in concussion protocol. Minnesota's Kyler Murray is week-to-week with a hamstring strain — a Week 10 return is possible, but the team has not confirmed it.
items.takeaway: Lock starts again in Seattle, rookie Carson Beck starts in Arizona, McCarthy is trending to play Thursday, and Watson is cleared for Sunday — Murray is still week-to-week.

items.headline: Weather: no game today, and Thursday is outdoors
paragraphs: There is no NFL game today, so there is nothing to forecast for. Week 10 opens Thursday night with Washington at the New York Giants, 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford — an outdoor stadium. The kickoff-window forecast is still two days out, so it gets checked again on Thursday, when it is actually useful.
items.takeaway: No game today; Thursday night at MetLife is outdoors, and the forecast gets a real check on Thursday.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — last week's cards are still showing, so Thursday goes through Check
paragraphs: The app board still shows Week 8. It was generated November 2 and I checked again this morning — it is the same board as last night, byte for byte. The headline cards on it are from last Monday night's Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. The Seahawks moneyline is the example: the model gave Seattle a 56.1% chance to win, while the -175 price needs 63.6% to break even, so the evaluator's expected value is negative. That is the point — Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the model at 50.6% against a market that priced Chicago at 46.5%, for a small positive edge.

One more thing the board has not picked up: it still shows Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter, from a stale Week 8 snapshot. Carson Wentz is the one who started Monday night — that comes from the team, not the app. Until the board flips to Week 10, there is no card to read for Thursday, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Commanders-Giants, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Thursday game? Thursday check.
items.takeaway: The board still shows last week's Week 8 cards and still lists Murray as Minnesota's starter, so Thursday's Commanders-Giants price goes through Check — type in your book's line and price and let the app give you a verdict on it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value — did you beat the market, or just win the bet?
paragraphs: Closing line value is a simple idea. It asks whether the price you took was better than the price the game closed at. If you bet a team at -3 and the line closes at -4.5, you got closing line value — you bought the same bet cheaper than the market ended up pricing it.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take a favorite at -3 at -110 on Tuesday. By kickoff on Thursday, the same favorite is -4.5. Your bet is already in a better spot than anyone who waited — if the favorite wins by exactly 4, you win and they push. If the favorite wins by 3, you push and they lose. Same team, same game — the only difference is when you bought the price.

Winning a bet and beating the closing line are two different things, and over a season, beating the closing line is the better sign that your process is working. A win can be luck. Consistently getting a better number than the close is a skill — it means you are reading the market before it moves, not after.
items.takeaway: Beating the closing line means you bought a better price than the market ended up at — over a season, that is a better sign your process works than any single win.

items.headline: Monday's numbers moved twice and both moves held — Thursday opens with the Giants -1.5
paragraphs: Monday's lines moved twice during the day. The Bills were -3 in the morning and closed at -3.5 at most books. The total fell four points during the week to 43.5 in the morning, then climbed back to 45.5 by kickoff. Both moves held up: Buffalo won by 17, so the favorite covered, and the game finished at 29 combined points, so the under cashed easily. The morning's 43.5 total is gone for good.

The next number to watch is Thursday's. The Week 10 opener has the Giants -1.5 over Washington, with a total of 44.5 to 45.5 depending on the book. That line was posted before Monday night, so it has not yet reacted to anything from Week 9's final game — and the Giants' quarterback is still the open question in it.

The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2, and there is no Commanders-Giants game on it at all. If your book's Thursday number looks different from the opener above, run it through Check and let the app judge your price, not last week's.
items.takeaway: Bills -3 to -3.5 and the total 43.5 to 45.5 on Monday — both moves held; Thursday opens Giants -1.5, total 44.5 to 45.5.

items.headline: No game today — use the quiet day to get Thursday's price right
paragraphs: There is no football today, and that is the point. Use the quiet day to look at Thursday's number early. If your book has the Giants at -1.5 or better and Check says bet, bet the good number now — a good number today beats a hoped-for number on Thursday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.

Wait only if your bet depends on a name that is still undecided. The one name is J.J. McCarthy: his hip is the question in Thursday's game, and the inactives come out about 90 minutes before kickoff. If your Thursday bet needs McCarthy to play, wait for the injury news. If it does not, there is nothing left to wait for.

One last thing. Settlement is manual — there is no auto-settle, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log Monday's losers too, not just the winners. A tracker that only remembers the wins is a story, not a record.
items.takeaway: No game today — if Check says bet on your Thursday number, bet it now; wait only if your bet needs McCarthy, whose status is decided by the inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff. And log Monday's losers too.

evidence.fact: Bills 23, Vikings 6 — Monday Night Football, Monday Nov 9, U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis. Buffalo improves to 7-1, Minnesota falls to 6-2 with a second straight loss. Josh Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. James Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards and a late touchdown. Carson Wentz started for Minnesota with Kyler Murray out (hamstring) and completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions. Buffalo held the ball for 42:32 and forced three turnovers. The game closed with Buffalo -3.5 and a total of 45.5, so the favorite covered and the total went under (29 combined points).
evidence.interpretation: Week 9 is closed. Buffalo won ugly against the league's heaviest-blitzing defense, and Minnesota's quarterback problem is now the story of its season.
evidence.app_guidance: Monday's game is settled — the numbers to watch now are Thursday's, when the board flips to Week 10.

evidence.fact: Quarterback and injury news overnight, Monday Nov 9 into Tuesday Nov 10: Seattle QB Sam Darnold is ruled out of the Week 10 game at Las Vegas on Nov 15 (quadriceps and a cracked rib); head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed it Monday, and Darnold is expected back after the Week 11 bye, in Week 12 against the 49ers. Drew Lock starts again for Seattle, though he is managing an oblique injury and elbow tendinitis. Arizona QB Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL and may be done for the season; the Cardinals signed 40-year-old QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad, and rookie Carson Beck is slated to start Week 10 against the Rams. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) is trending toward playing Thursday night against Washington, per head coach John Harbaugh; he missed part of Sunday's win over the Eagles but returned. Browns QB Deshaun Watson has been cleared to play Sunday against Houston after missing last week in concussion protocol. Vikings QB Kyler Murray (hamstring strain) is week-to-week with no confirmed return date; a Week 10 return is possible but not confirmed.
evidence.interpretation: Two starting-quarterback changes for Week 10 are now set — Lock again in Seattle, Beck in Arizona — while Thursday's Giants starter is the one name still to be confirmed.
evidence.app_guidance: These are Week 10 facts. They matter when the board flips and the new prices appear — and for Thursday, McCarthy's status is the name to watch before betting.

evidence.fact: There is no NFL game on Tuesday Nov 10. Week 10 opens Thursday Nov 12 with Washington at the New York Giants, 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — an outdoor stadium. The kickoff-window forecast for Thursday is still two days out and will be checked again closer to the game.
